why: The JSONL ledger earns its keep as shared data (written by `add`, mutated by mutate.py --spec refute, tagged by lane for a multi-session setup) -- pytest can't do that. But most of the 500 lines duplicate, imperfectly, distinctions pytest's 5-way exit code already makes for free: both bugs motivating this file are exactly the class pytest's design avoids. Per house rule ('a dependency that deletes hundreds of lines wins') and pytest costing nothing new here: keep the ledger schema, replace dispatch/reporting/selftest with a thin conftest.py.

alternatives.gap: no native concept of a claims ledger as external JSONL data other non-Python processes (bus.py, other Claude sessions, ad hoc `refute.py add`) append to at runtime; pytest tests live in .py source.

what_ours_does: refute.py: CLI (run/add/list/selftest) loading named claims+verifiers from state/claims-verify.jsonl, running each via pwsh/Git-Bash, classifying HELD/REFUTED/BROKEN (BROKEN=verifier failed to launch/timed out, unlike a claim that ran and failed). Exit=refuted+broken, capped 125. Ships its own selftest planting synthetic ledgers, locking down two real 2026-07-25 bugs in its exit-code logic.
strongest_counterargument: Rewriting adds a second execution model for a 'one maintainer, read by one person' repo. The current file is flat and already-debugged: both incidents that motivated it are regression-locked by its own selftest, and mutate.py already mutation-tests its exit logic. Migration risks new seam bugs for a real but not urgent line-count win on a tool that isn't broken today.
